name: Bhavabhuti
bio: Bhavabhuti was a Sanskrit dramatist of the early eighth century AD, ranked beside Kalidasa among the great playwrights of classical India. By his own account, given in the prologues of his plays, he belonged to a learned Brahmin family of Vidarbha and was the son of Nilakantha and Jatukarni; he is associated with the court of King Yashovarman of Kanyakubja (Kannauj).

Three plays are attributed to him: the Mahaviracharita and the Malatimadhava, which treat the heroic and the romantic, and the Uttararamacharita, which dramatises the last part of the story of Rama. He is especially admired for the depth of feeling, and the pathos, of that last play. Here the Uttararamacharita appears in the original Sanskrit.
